concept.name: XGBoost
concept.definition: A scalable gradient-tree-boosting system using a regularized objective, second-order loss approximation, sparsity-aware split handling, and optimized tree construction.
concept.intuition: It is a learnable mapping or representation used to turn features into predictions or groups.
concept.mechanics: At each boosting round, use gradients and Hessians to choose tree splits and leaf weights, add the regularized tree, and update predictions.
concept.formula: Prediction = sum of tree leaf scores; objective = loss + sum of tree penalties
concept.failure_modes: Flexible models can fit noise, shift under new regimes, and conceal instability when tuning is repeated on the same validation data.
concept.misconceptions: Greater model complexity or in-sample accuracy does not by itself imply better out-of-sample trading results.
concept.example: A binary classifier adds 200 shallow trees at learning rate 0.05 and converts the summed margin through a logistic link.

citations.source: Chen and Guestrin, XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
citations.section: Regularized objective and gradient tree boosting
